quickClean.title: Quick Clean
quickClean.description: Empty trash and user cache instantly, no password needed.
quickClean.confirmBody: This empties the trash and the user cache. This can't be undone.

fullClean.title: Full Clean
fullClean.description: Everything above, plus Flatpak, Snap, temp files, APT cache and logs.
fullClean.confirmBody: This cleans every safe category at once (trash, user cache, unused Flatpak runtimes, old Snap revisions, temp files, APT cache and logs). Installed apps are left untouched — that needs picking which ones by hand. May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

trash.title: Trash
trash.confirmBody: This permanently deletes {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} ({size}) from the Trash. This can't be undone.

cache.title: User Cache
cache.confirmBody: This permanently deletes {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} ({size}) from ~/.cache. This can't be undone.

flatpak.title: Unused Flatpak runtimes
flatpak.confirmBody: This permanently uninstalls {count, plural, one {# runtime} other {# runtimes}} ({size}) no installed Flatpak app still uses. May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

snap.title: Old Snap revisions
snap.confirmBody: This permanently removes {count, plural, one {# disabled revision} other {# disabled revisions}} ({size}) Snap keeps around for rollback. May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

apps.title: Installed apps
apps.confirmBody: This permanently uninstalls {count, plural, one {# app} other {# apps}} ({size}). Configuration files are kept. May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

aptCache.title: APT package cache
aptCache.confirmBody: This permanently deletes {count, plural, one {# downloaded .deb package} other {# downloaded .deb packages}} ({size}) from /var/cache/apt/archives. May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

temp.title: Temporary files
temp.confirmBody: This permanently deletes {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} ({size}) from /tmp or /var/tmp. May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

logs.title: System logs
logs.confirmBody: This shrinks the journald log to the last 7 days (currently {size}). May ask for an administrator password. This can't be undone.

page.exportListHint: Save a script that installs these apps again after a format (APT, Flatpak and Snap). The AppImages are listed in it with their address, to download by hand.
page.exportListDone: List exported: {count, plural, one {# app} other {# apps}}
page.exportListFailed: The list could not be exported
page.userNote: No password: only files owned by your user.
page.failed: {name}: the cleanup failed or was cancelled. Nothing was recorded for it.

kernels.title: Kernels
kernels.description: Old kernels with their headers and source, and leftovers of removed kernels. The kernel in use and the newest other one are always kept.
kernels.concept: Every kernel installed besides the one you are running. Removing one also removes its image, headers and source packages.
kernels.keep: The running kernel and the newest other kernel, always. Kernels installed by hand are never treated as leftovers.
kernels.noteRunning: Protected: this is the kernel in use.
kernels.noteReserve: Protected: the newest other kernel is always kept as a fallback.
kernels.noteOld: Removes its image, headers and source packages.
kernels.noteOrphanDir: Left behind by a kernel that is no longer installed.
kernels.noteOrphanKbuild: No installed kernel uses this package.

drivers.title: Drivers
drivers.description: Drivers and tools for hardware this machine does not have, and orphaned DKMS builds.
drivers.concept: Graphics stacks, printer drivers, hypervisor guest tools and similar packages whose hardware was not detected here. Removing one also rebuilds the initramfs.
drivers.keep: Anything for hardware that is present, the guest tools of the hypervisor this machine runs on, and remote clients such as virt-viewer.
drivers.noteAbsent: The hardware this package serves was not detected on this machine.
drivers.noteDkms: Its source package is gone: these compiled modules are leftovers.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.description: Firmware files for hardware this machine does not have.
firmware.concept: Firmware under /lib/firmware. A family is listed as removable only when no detection layer claims it: PCI and USB devices, loaded drivers, the kernel log and the dracut configuration.
firmware.keep: Everything this hardware uses, and any family whose driver is still installed. Removing firmware also rebuilds the initramfs.
firmware.noteHardware: Protected: the hardware of this machine uses it.
firmware.noteDriver: Protected: its driver is still installed. Remove the driver first.
firmware.noteUnused: No detected hardware uses this firmware.

simulation.blocked: Blocked: the removal would also remove {name}, which the system needs.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Translations, desktop help and translated manual pages of languages you do not use.
languages.concept: One row per language, with its regional variants grouped. Removing a language deletes its translations, desktop and KDE help and translated manual pages.
languages.keep: Your active language, its fallback codes and English, always. When your language is kept, its other regional variants can still be removed.
languages.noteActive: Protected: this is your active language.
languages.noteEnglish: Protected: English is the fallback of every program.
languages.noteKeeps: Your active variant is kept; only the other regional variants go.
languages.noteUnused: Removes its translations, help and translated manual pages. They return when their packages are upgraded.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.description: Package documentation folders and documentation stores. Copyright files are always kept.
docs.concept: The documentation folders of packages that take over 1 MB under /usr/share/doc, plus Info pages, Qt, GTK-Doc and Devhelp documentation.
docs.keep: The copyright files of every package, the Info index, and the manual pages. The whole /usr/share/doc and /usr/share/man are never offered.
docs.noteBack: Comes back when the package is upgraded or reinstalled.

detection.firmwareNote: Protected: hardware detection is unavailable. Install pciutils, usbutils and kmod.
detection.driversNote: Without pciutils, usbutils and kmod nothing can be judged unused, so no package is listed.

basic.subtitle: Check and clean your system safely.
basic.shortcutAdd: Add a launcher for the advanced version
basic.shortcutAdded: Launcher added to the applications menu
basic.advancedMissing: The advanced version was not found.
basic.confirmBody: About {size} will be freed. Only what is safe to remove is cleaned.
basic.otherVersion: Another version of Sys Cleaner was opened. Close this one first.

residual.title: Residual configuration
residual.description: Packages that were removed but left their configuration files behind (dpkg state rc).
residual.concept: Packages that are no longer installed but kept their configuration files in the system, which happens when a package is removed and not purged. Purging deletes those files.
residual.keep: Installed packages and everything in your home folder. If you install one of these packages again it starts with its default settings.
residual.note: Not installed; only its configuration is left. Purging deletes it for good.
residual.noteSystem: Login screen, boot loader or base of the system: it is not purged, because its purge script can delete files other packages use.

orphans.title: Orphaned packages
orphans.description: Packages installed as dependencies that nothing needs any more: what apt autoremove would remove.
orphans.concept: Packages that were installed only because another package needed them, and that no installed package needs now. apt itself provides the list.
orphans.keep: Everything else. The full list of what would be removed is shown first, and the cleanup is blocked if it would also remove something the system needs.
orphans.note: Nothing installed needs it now: check the list before removing.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Get a desktop notification when a cleanup is due. It only notifies: it never cleans anything by itself.
alerts.stateOn: On: the check is scheduled. You decide what to clean when you open the program.
alerts.stateOff: Off: no service is installed and no notification will be sent.
alerts.turnedOff: Alerts are off and the service was removed
alerts.testFailed: The notification could not be sent: {error}
alerts.byTimeHint: Notifies when this much time has passed since the last cleanup.
alerts.byWeightHint: Notifies when this much is ready to clean, which is what the standard cleanup would free.
alerts.checkHint: How often the program looks. A shorter time notices sooner but scans more often.
alerts.invalid: Fill in every value of the options you turn on, and how often to check.
alerts.desktopNote: The notification appears on any desktop. Some desktops open the program when you click it; on the others, open it from the applications menu.
alerts.notifyTime: Days since the last cleanup: {days}. Open Soplos Sys Cleaner to review.
alerts.notifyWeight: Ready to clean: {size}. Open Soplos Sys Cleaner to review.
alerts.notifyTest: This is a test notification. If you can read it, the alerts will reach you.

journal.title: Journal retention
journal.nothing: Nothing to free with this retention
journal.estimateNote: Approximate: removes archived journal files beyond the retention.
journal.unknownNote: The amount cannot be estimated: it frees whatever exceeds the retention.

notes.slowRebuild: It regenerates, but rebuilding it costs time on the next launch.
notes.manualApp: You installed this yourself: check whether you still use it.
notes.recentTemp: Changed in the last day: it may still be in use.
notes.snapApp: Removing it uninstalls the whole snap.
notes.appImageApp: Deletes the file, its launcher and its icon.
notes.cacheSocket: In use: a program keeps its live connection here. It is not cleaned.
notes.cacheLock: In use: it holds lock or process files of a program. It is not cleaned.
notes.cacheOpen: In use: a running program has it open. It is not cleaned.

trash.concept: Files you already deleted. Emptying the trash frees their space for good.
trash.keep: Only the trash is emptied; no other folder is touched.

cache.concept: Data that apps rebuild on their own in ~/.cache. There are never documents here.
cache.keep: Cookies, passwords and profiles live in ~/.mozilla or ~/.config, not in .cache: they are not touched.

flatpak.concept: Runtimes and extensions that no installed app needs. Every major update leaves the previous runtime behind.
flatpak.keep: Installed apps and the runtimes they use.

snap.concept: Snap keeps several revisions of each package. Disabled ones are not used and only take up disk space.
snap.keep: The active revision of every snap is never listed.

apps.concept: Applications you installed by hand: APT packages, Flatpak and Snap apps, and AppImages in ~/AppImages. Removing one uninstalls it; its configuration files are kept. Export reinstall script saves a script that installs them again after a format (APT, Flatpak and Snap); the AppImages are listed in it with their download address.
apps.keep: Anything not installed manually. Nothing is selected by default. Flatpak runtimes and base snaps have their own pages.

temp.concept: Files and folders in /tmp and /var/tmp. Those changed in the last day may still be in use, so they are marked Review.
temp.keep: Sockets, pipes, symbolic links and systemd private directories are skipped.

aptCache.concept: The .deb packages apt downloaded. They can be downloaded again at any time; reinstalling only costs bandwidth.
aptCache.keep: Installed packages and the repository lists.

logs.concept: The systemd journal. Cleaning keeps only the last 7 days of logs.
logs.keep: The last 7 days of logs, including the current session.

history.failedDetail: The cleanup failed or was cancelled. Nothing was freed.
history.noDetail: No receipt: this entry was recorded before receipts existed.
history.exportFailed: The CSV could not be exported
history.conceptBody: Audit log: what was cleaned, when and how much it freed. Nothing happens behind your back.

cacheView.empty: Nothing to clean in the user cache.

about.tagline: Scan and clean your Soplos Linux system with a clear preview before anything is removed.
